name: AZ-09
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+15 district with incumbent Paul Gosar running again
Prediction markets price a Republican hold near 94%
Sterbinsky trails badly in cash on hand (~$26k vs ~$303k)
No public polls or expert ratings; environment already assumed Democratic-leaning
model.rationale: The seat sits in a deeply Republican district that Gosar has held easily, and the challenger's modest fundraising and thin cash position give her little visible path. Markets price a Republican hold near certainty, and even a favorable national environment only trims the district's heavy lean.
model.watch: A wave of Democratic outside spending or a poll showing Gosar well below majority support would be the first sign of a genuine contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Arizona's 9th district leans heavily Republican, and Paul Gosar has held the seat since 2013 without a close general election. He runs again with about $303,000 in the bank after raising roughly $580,000, while Democrat Dani Sterbinsky has raised about $354,000 but reports only around $26,000 cash on hand. Outside spending on either side has been negligible so far.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give the Republican roughly a 94% chance of holding the seat. The district's partisan lean points to a comfortable Republican margin even after accounting for a national environment that favors Democrats. Sterbinsky would need a major influx of money or attention to become competitive; the current evidence points to Gosar returning for another term.
